datasets.title: Guinea: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/gin-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR biophysical measurements from VIIRS satellite observations are composited into 10-day intervals. FAPAR anomalies are calculated at each grid cell by computing the deviation from a long-term mean baseline (2012 to most recent full year), producing raster datasets that serve as an empirical indicator of agricultural drought stress on vegetation.

sources.name: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: Copernicus Vegetation Index program providing FAPAR biophysical measurements from VIIRS satellite radiometer data processed into 10-day composites with long-term baseline anomaly calculations
